statements.subject: session
statements.description: RTSP 2.0 first establishes a context including content resources (the media) — Session Establishment is one of RTSP's three fundamental parts.

statements.subject: session
statements.description: RTSP 2.0 then controls the delivery of content resources from the provider to the consumer — Media Delivery Control is one of RTSP's three fundamental parts.

statements.subject: session
statements.description: RTSP 2.0 first establishes a context including content resources (the media) and then controls the delivery of these content resources from the provider to the consumer.

statements.subject: client
statements.description: The client creates an RTSP session by sending a request using the SETUP method to the server. In the Transport header of the SETUP request, the client also includes all the transport parameters necessary to enable the media delivery protocol to function.
actions: include Transport header with transport parameters

statements.subject: session
statements.description: When receiving a SETUP request, the server determines if the media resource is available and if one or more of the transport parameter specifications are acceptable. If that is successful, an RTSP session context is created and the relevant parameters and state is stored. An identifier is created for the RTSP session and included in the response in the Session header.
statements.trigger: SETUP request received with available media resource and acceptable transport parameters
actions: send SETUP response with Session header
send SETUP response with Transport header

statements.subject: session
statements.description: A SETUP request that references an existing RTSP session but identifies a new media resource is a request to add that media resource under common control with the already-present media resources in an aggregated session.
statements.trigger: SETUP request referencing existing session with new media resource
actions: add new media resource to existing session under common control

statements.subject: session
statements.description: To avoid an extra round trip in the session establishment of aggregated RTSP sessions, RTSP 2.0 supports pipelined requests; i.e., the client can send multiple requests back-to-back without waiting first for the completion of any of them. The client uses a client-selected identifier in the Pipelined-Requests header to instruct the server to bind multiple requests together as if they included the session identifier.
statements.trigger: pipelined SETUP requests sent with Pipelined-Requests header
actions: include Pipelined-Requests header with client-selected identifier
server binds requests together as if they included session identifier

statements.subject: session
statements.description: After having established an RTSP session, the client can start controlling the media delivery.

statements.subject: session
statements.description: begin playback, using the PLAY method

statements.subject: session
statements.description: suspend (pause) playback by using the PAUSE method

statements.subject: session
statements.description: After having established an RTSP session, the client can start controlling the media delivery. The basic operations are 'begin playback', using the PLAY method.
actions: begin media delivery from specified or default position

statements.subject: session
statements.description: If the client issues a PAUSE, the delivery will be halted and the point at which the server stopped will be reported back in the response.
actions: report stopped position in PAUSE response

statements.subject: session
statements.description: The client can later resume by sending a PLAY request without a Range header.
actions: resume media delivery from halted position

statements.subject: session
statements.description: When the server is about to complete the PLAY request by delivering the end of the content or the requested range, the server will send a PLAY_NOTIFY request indicating this.
statements.trigger: end of content or end of requested range reached
actions: send PLAY_NOTIFY request indicating impending completion

statements.subject: session
statements.description: delivery continues until the client sends a PAUSE request, tears down the session, or the content ends.

statements.subject: session
statements.description: If the live transmission ends, the server must send a PLAY_NOTIFY request with the updated Media-Properties indicating that the content stopped being a recorded live session and instead became on-demand content; the request also contains the final media range.

statements.subject: session
statements.description: The properties applicable for the RTSP session are provided by the server in the SETUP response using the Media-Properties header.

statements.subject: server
statements.description: When the server wants to notify the client about the completion of the media delivery, it sends a PLAY_NOTIFY request to the client.

statements.subject: server
statements.description: The PLAY_NOTIFY request includes information about the stream end, including the last RTP sequence number for each stream, thus enabling the client to empty the buffer smoothly.
actions: client empties buffer using last RTP sequence number per stream

statements.subject: session
statements.description: The session context that has been established is kept alive by having the client show liveness.

statements.subject: session
statements.description: The session context is terminated by client TEARDOWN, removal of all media resources, session timeout expiry, or server-initiated TEARDOWN.

statements.subject: session
statements.description: If the client fails to show liveness for more than the established session timeout value (normally 60 seconds), the server may terminate the context.

statements.subject: session
statements.description: The session context is normally terminated by the client sending a TEARDOWN request to the server referencing the aggregated control URI.
actions: client sends TEARDOWN referencing aggregated control URI

statements.subject: session
statements.description: If all media resources are removed from a session context, the session context is terminated.

statements.subject: session
statements.description: When a server terminates the session context, it does so by sending a TEARDOWN request indicating the reason.
actions: server sends TEARDOWN request with Terminate-Reason

statements.subject: session
statements.description: A server can request that the client tear down the session and re-establish it at an alternative server using the REDIRECT method; the client needs to initiate session termination prior to the deadline.
actions: server sends REDIRECT with Terminate-Reason header
server includes Location header if alternative server available
client initiates session termination prior to deadline
client re-establishes session at alternative server

statements.subject: session
statements.description: When the deadline expires, the server simply stops providing the service.

statements.subject: session
statements.description: In case the server has no other server to redirect to, and it wants to close the session for maintenance, it shall use the TEARDOWN method with a Terminate-Reason header.

statements.subject: session
statements.description: It is established by an RTSP server upon the completion of a successful SETUP request (when a 200 OK response is sent) and is labeled with a session identifier at that time.
statements.trigger: SETUP request completes with 200 OK response sent

statements.subject: session
statements.description: The session exists until timed out by the server or explicitly removed by a TEARDOWN request.

statements.subject: session
statements.description: The session exists until timed out by the server or explicitly removed by a TEARDOWN request.

statements.subject: session
statements.description: An RTSP session is a stateful entity; an RTSP server maintains an explicit session state machine (see Appendix B) where most state transitions are triggered by client requests.
statements.guard_semantics: most state transitions are triggered by client requests

statements.subject: transaction
statements.description: After receiving and interpreting a request message, the recipient responds with an RTSP response message. Normally, there is only one, final, response.

statements.subject: transaction
statements.description: Responses using the response code class 1xx is the only class for which there MAY be sent one or more responses prior to the final response message.

statements.subject: connection
statements.description: RTSP requests can be transmitted using the two different connection scenarios listed below: persistent - a transport connection is used for several request/response transactions; transient - a transport connection is used for each single request/response transaction.

statements.subject: connection
statements.description: This transport connection uses TCP or TCP/TLS. RTSP requests MUST NOT be sent to multicast groups since no connection can be established with a specific receiver in multicast environments.

statements.subject: connection
statements.description: transient - a transport connection is used for each single request/response transaction.

statements.subject: connection
statements.description: persistent - a transport connection is used for several request/response transactions.

statements.subject: session
statements.description: An RTSP agent SHALL NOT use more than one connection per RTSP session at any given point.
statements.guard_semantics: At most one TCP connection per RTSP session may be active at any given point in time

statements.subject: connection
statements.description: When the client has discovered that the TCP connection has been lost, it can set up a new one when there is need to communicate again.
statements.trigger: TCP connection loss detected & new communication needed

statements.subject: server
statements.description: A server that attempts to send a request to a client that has no connection currently to the server SHALL discard the request.
statements.trigger: server attempts to send request to client

statements.subject: connection
statements.description: When under attack, an RTSP agent can close TCP connections and release state associated with that TCP connection.
actions: release state associated with TCP connection

statements.subject: connection
statements.description: A persistent connection MAY be closed after a few message exchanges. Later, when the client wishes to send a new request, a new connection would be opened.
statements.trigger: client wishes to send new request after persistent connection closed

statements.subject: endpoint
statements.description: To avoid deadlock situations, both client and server MUST be able to send and receive requests simultaneously.
statements.guard_semantics: Endpoint must support concurrent send and receive to avoid deadlock

statements.subject: client
statements.description: The client MAY close a connection at any point when no outstanding request/response transactions exist for any RTSP session being managed through the connection.

statements.subject: server
statements.description: The server SHOULD NOT close a connection until all RTSP sessions being managed through the connection have been timed out.

statements.subject: server
statements.description: A server SHOULD NOT close a connection immediately after responding to a session-level TEARDOWN request for the last RTSP session being controlled through the connection. The server SHOULD wait at least 10 seconds after sending the TEARDOWN response before closing the connection.
statements.trigger: 10 seconds elapsed after TEARDOWN response sent for last session
actions: wait at least 10 seconds after TEARDOWN response

statements.subject: server
statements.description: The server MAY close a connection if it receives an incomplete message and if the message is not completed within a reasonable amount of time. It is RECOMMENDED that the server wait at least 10 seconds for the completion of a message.

statements.subject: client
statements.description: If a server closes a connection while the client is attempting to send a new request, the client will have to close its current connection, establish a new connection, and send its request over the new connection.
statements.trigger: server closes connection while client is sending new request

statements.subject: connection
statements.description: A server closes a connection after initiating the connection closing procedure following TEARDOWN or session timeout.

statements.subject: server
statements.description: A server SHOULD NOT close the connection directly as a result of responding to a request with an error code.

statements.subject: transaction
statements.description: If the responder recognizes that the processing of a request will take longer than 5 seconds, it SHOULD send a 100 (Continue) response as soon as possible. It SHOULD continue sending a 100 response every 5 seconds thereafter until it is ready to send the final response to the requester.
statements.trigger: 5-second response timer expiry while processing request

statements.subject: transaction
statements.description: After sending a 100 response, the responder MUST send a final response indicating the success or failure of the request.
statements.trigger: ready to finalize after having sent 100 (Continue)
actions: send final response indicating success or failure

statements.subject: transaction
statements.description: After receiving a 100 response, the requester SHOULD continue waiting for further responses.

statements.subject: connection
statements.description: A requester SHOULD wait at least 10 seconds for a response before concluding that the responder will not be responding to its request. If more than 10 seconds elapse without receiving any response, the requester MAY assume that the responder is unresponsive and abort the connection by closing the TCP connection.
statements.trigger: 10-second timeout expiry with no response received

statements.subject: connection
statements.description: the RTSP client or server SHOULD establish a new connection and send any requests that are queued up or that haven't received a response on this new connection.
statements.trigger: request abandoned and old TCP connection closed
actions: send queued or unanswered requests on new connection

statements.subject: session
statements.description: the RTSP agent SHOULD send a keep-alive request, if no other request will be sent immediately for that RTSP session, for each RTSP session on the old connection. The keep-alive request will normally be a SET_PARAMETER with a session header to inform the server that this agent cares about this RTSP session.
statements.trigger: new connection established, no immediate request pending for RTSP session previously on old connection
actions: send SET_PARAMETER with session header as keep-alive for each affected RTSP session

statements.subject: session
statements.description: established session — the length of the session timeout MUST NOT be changed in an established session

statements.subject: session
statements.description: RTSP requires the client to periodically show its liveness to the server or the server may terminate any session state … closing the session due to lack of activity

statements.subject: session
statements.description: The timeout parameter of the Session header MAY be included in a SETUP response and MUST NOT be included in requests. The server uses it to indicate to the client how long the server is prepared to wait between RTSP commands or other signs of life before closing the session due to lack of activity.
statements.guard_semantics: MAY appear in SETUP response; MUST NOT appear in any request

statements.subject: session
statements.description: The length of the session timeout MUST NOT be changed in an established session.

statements.subject: client
statements.description: To show liveness between RTSP requests, mechanisms (RTCP, SET_PARAMETER, GET_PARAMETER, OPTIONS) can be used; client SHOULD NOT wait to the last second of the timeout before trying to send a liveness message.
statements.trigger: liveness keep-alive sent (RTCP / SET_PARAMETER / GET_PARAMETER / OPTIONS)

statements.subject: client
statements.description: In such a situation, where none of the RTSP servers/proxies/addresses can handle the request, the RTSP agent has to wait before it can send any new requests to the RTSP server.

statements.subject: client
statements.description: Any additional request to a specific address MUST be delayed according to the Retry-After headers received.

statements.subject: timer
statements.description: For addresses where no response was received or TCP timeout occurred, an initial wait timer SHOULD be set to 5 seconds.

statements.subject: timer
statements.description: That timer MUST be doubled for each additional failure to connect or receive response until the value exceeds 30 minutes when the timer's mean value may be set to 30 minutes.

statements.subject: timer
statements.description: Until the value exceeds 30 minutes when the timer's mean value may be set to 30 minutes. It is REQUIRED not to set the same value in the timer for each scheduling, but instead to add a variation to the mean value, resulting in picking a random value within the range of 0.5 to 1.5 times the mean value.

statements.subject: timer
statements.description: For addresses where no response was received or TCP timeout occurred, an initial wait timer SHOULD be set to 5 seconds. That timer MUST be doubled for each additional failure.
statements.guard_semantics: Controls delay before next connection attempt after TCP timeout or no response; doubles on each additional failure up to 30-minute mean

statements.subject: server
statements.description: The OPTIONS response MUST contain a Public header that declares all methods supported for the indicated resource.
actions: send OPTIONS response with Public header listing all supported methods

statements.subject: endpoint
statements.description: If the receiver of the request does not support the method, it will respond with an error code indicating the method is either not implemented (501) or does not apply for the resource (405).

statements.subject: endpoint
statements.description: The endpoint receiving a request containing a Require MUST negatively acknowledge any feature that it does not understand and not perform the request. The response in cases where features are not supported is 551 (Option Not Supported). Also, the features that are not supported are given in the Unsupported header in the response.
statements.trigger: request received with Require header containing unsupported feature
actions: include Unsupported header listing unsupported features
do not perform the requested operation

statements.subject: message
statements.description: Proxies are required to add this header (Proxy-Supported) whenever the Supported header is present.

statements.subject: session
statements.description: The Pipelined-Request header allows a client to request that two or more requests be processed in the same RTSP session context that the first request creates.
statements.guard_semantics: enables shared session context across pipelined requests

statements.subject: server
statements.description: The responding agent MUST process the incoming requests in their sending order. The processing of the request MUST also have been finished before processing the next request from the same agent. The responses MUST be sent in the order the requests were processed.
actions: complete current request before processing next

statements.subject: client
statements.description: In case one of the SETUP requests fails unexpectedly, the PLAY request can still be successfully executed. However, the resulting presentation will not be as expected by the requesting client, as only a single media instead of two will be played. In this case, the client can send a PAUSE request, correct the failing SETUP request, and then request it be played.
statements.trigger: pipelined SETUP failure detected after PLAY executed

statements.subject: session
statements.description: PAUSE is required because it is the only way of leaving the Play state without terminating the whole session.

statements.subject: session
statements.description: PAUSE is required because it is the only way of leaving the Play state without terminating the whole session.
actions: leave Play state without terminating session

statements.subject: session
statements.description: PAUSE is the only way of leaving the Play state without terminating the whole session — implying TEARDOWN leaves the Play state by terminating the whole session.

statements.subject: server
statements.description: If an RTSP agent does not support a particular method, it MUST return a 501 (Not Implemented) response code and the requesting RTSP agent, in turn, SHOULD NOT try this method again for the given agent/resource combination.

statements.subject: session
statements.description: An OPTIONS request may be issued at any time. Such a request does not modify the session state.

statements.subject: session
statements.description: The OPTIONS method can be used to keep an RTSP session alive. However, it may prolong the session lifespan.

statements.subject: session
statements.description: An OPTIONS request intended for keeping alive an RTSP session MUST include the Session header with the associated session identifier.
statements.guard_semantics: Only applies when OPTIONS is used for session keep-alive

statements.subject: session
statements.description: The DESCRIBE reply-response pair constitutes the media initialization phase of RTSP.

statements.subject: client
statements.description: The DESCRIBE reply-response pair constitutes the media initialization phase of RTSP. The server MUST respond with a description of the requested resource and return the description in the message body of the response, if the DESCRIBE method request can be successfully fulfilled.
actions: server returns description in message body

statements.subject: client
statements.description: If a client obtains a valid description from an alternate source, the client MAY use this description for initialization purposes without issuing a DESCRIBE request for the same media.
statements.trigger: valid description obtained from alternate source
actions: client uses alternate description for initialization without issuing DESCRIBE request

statements.subject: session
statements.description: Init: Initial state. No session exists.

statements.subject: session
statements.description: Ready: Session is ready to start playing.

statements.subject: session
statements.description: Play: Session is playing, i.e., sending media-stream data in the direction S->C.

statements.subject: session
statements.description: Init and Ready can also be used for the creation of the RTSP session. A successful SETUP in Init creates the session and moves to Ready.

statements.subject: session
statements.description: SETUP can be used in Ready state to change the transport parameters of media streams that are already set up, or for creation of the RTSP session.

statements.subject: session
statements.description: SETUP can be used in Play state to change the transport parameters of media streams that are already set up.

statements.subject: session
statements.description: If a SETUP request on a session fails for any reason, the session state, as well as transport and other parameters for associated streams, MUST remain unchanged from their values as if the SETUP request had never been received by the server.

statements.subject: server
statements.description: The server MUST generate a session identifier in response to a successful SETUP request unless a SETUP request to a server includes a session identifier or a Pipelined-Requests header referencing an existing session context.

statements.subject: session
statements.description: A session will exist until it is either removed by a TEARDOWN request or is timed out by the server. The server MAY remove a session that has not demonstrated liveness signs from the client(s) within a certain timeout period. The default timeout value is 60 seconds.

statements.subject: server
statements.description: If a SETUP request to a server includes a session identifier referencing an existing session context, the server MUST bundle this SETUP request into the existing session (aggregated session) or return a 459 (Aggregate Operation Not Allowed) error code.
statements.trigger: SETUP request with existing session identifier
actions: bundle stream into existing aggregated session

statements.subject: client
statements.description: A client MAY issue a SETUP request for a stream that is already set up or playing in the session to change transport parameters, which a server MAY allow.

statements.subject: server
statements.description: If it does not allow the changing of parameters, it MUST respond with error 455 (Method Not Valid in This State).
actions: send 455 Method Not Valid in This State

statements.subject: client
statements.description: If a client receives a 455 error when trying to change transport parameters while the server is in Play state, it MAY try to put the server in Ready state using PAUSE before issuing the SETUP request again.

statements.subject: client
statements.description: If that also fails, the changing of transport parameters will require that the client perform a TEARDOWN of the affected media and then set it up again.
actions: client sends TEARDOWN for affected media

statements.subject: server
statements.description: In a SETUP response for a request to change the transport parameters while in Play state, the server MUST include the Range header to indicate at what point the new transport parameters will be used.

statements.subject: server
statements.description: If RTP is used for delivery, the server MUST also include the RTP-Info header to indicate at what timestamp and RTP sequence number the change will take place.

statements.subject: server
statements.description: If the transport-parameters change that happened while in Play state results in a change of synchronization-related information, for example, changing RTP SSRC, the server MUST include the necessary synchronization information in the SETUP response.
statements.trigger: SETUP (transport change causing sync info change)
actions: include synchronization information in SETUP response

statements.subject: session
statements.description: PLAY requests are valid when the session is in Ready or Play state.

statements.subject: session
statements.description: PLAY requests are valid when the session is in Ready or Play state.

statements.subject: session
statements.description: PLAY requests are valid when the session is in Ready or Play state. Upon receipt of the PLAY request, the server MUST position the normal play time to the beginning of the range specified and deliver stream data.
actions: position NPT to start of Range

statements.subject: session
statements.description: A PLAY request while the stream is still in the Play state is legal and can be issued without an intervening PAUSE request. Such a request MUST replace the current PLAY action with the new one requested, i.e., being handled in the same way as if the request was received in Ready state.
actions: replace current PLAY action with new PLAY request parameters

statements.subject: session
statements.description: After playing the desired range, the presentation does NOT change to the Ready state, media delivery simply stops. If it is necessary to put the stream into the Ready state, a PAUSE request MUST be issued.

statements.subject: session
statements.description: If it is necessary to put the stream into the Ready state, a PAUSE request MUST be issued.
actions: set pause point to current media position

statements.subject: session
statements.description: A PLAY request MUST include a Session header to indicate to which session the request applies.

statements.subject: server
statements.description: Servers MUST include a Range header in any PLAY response, even if no Range header was present in the request.

statements.subject: session
statements.description: PLAY requests are valid when the session is in Ready or Play state.

statements.subject: session
statements.description: In an aggregated session, the PLAY request MUST contain an aggregated control URI.

statements.subject: server
statements.description: A server MUST respond with a 460 error (Only Aggregate Operation Allowed) if the client PLAY Request-URI is for a single media on an aggregated session.
statements.trigger: PLAY request with single-media URI on aggregated session

statements.subject: client
statements.description: For aggregated sessions where the initial SETUP request (creating a session) is followed by one or more additional SETUP requests, a PLAY request MAY be pipelined after those additional SETUP requests without awaiting their responses.
statements.trigger: PLAY request pipelined after additional SETUP requests
statements.pre_cond: session.type = aggregated & session.initial_setup_done = true & session.additional_setups_sent = true
actions: pipeline PLAY after SETUP requests without awaiting SETUP responses

statements.subject: client
statements.description: In case of failure, the client can halt the media playout using PAUSE and try to establish the intended state again before issuing another PLAY request.
statements.trigger: failure detected in pipelined prior request responses

statements.subject: client
statements.description: After halting playout via PAUSE following a pipelined failure, the client issues another PLAY request once the intended state is re-established.
statements.trigger: PLAY request after re-establishing intended state

statements.subject: session
statements.description: Clients can issue PLAY requests while the stream is in Play state and thus updating their request.

statements.subject: session
statements.description: A total replacement is signaled by having the first range specification have an explicit start value, in which case the server stops playout at the current playout point and then starts delivering media according to the Range header. This is equivalent to having the client first send a PAUSE and then a new PLAY request that isn't based on the pause point.
statements.trigger: PLAY request with explicit range start value
actions: stop playout at current playout point
start delivering media per Range header

statements.subject: session
statements.description: In the case of continuation, the first range specifier has an implicit start point and an explicit stop value (Z), which indicate that it MUST convert the range specifier being played prior to this PLAY request (X to Y) into (X to Z) and continue as if this was the request originally played.
statements.trigger: PLAY request with implicit range start and explicit stop value
statements.pre_cond: session.state = Play & range.start = implicit & range.stop = explicit
actions: convert range specifier from (X to Y) to (X to Z)

statements.subject: server
statements.description: If the current delivery point is beyond the stop point, the server SHALL immediately pause delivery. As the request has been completed successfully, it shall be responded to with a 200 OK response. A PLAY_NOTIFY with end-of-stream is also sent to indicate the actual stop point. The pause point is set to the requested stop point.
statements.trigger: current delivery point beyond stop point
actions: set pause point to requested stop point

statements.subject: session
statements.description: A common use of a PLAY request while in Play state is changing the scale of the media, i.e., entering or leaving fast forward or fast rewind. The client can issue an updating PLAY request that is either a continuation or a complete replacement.
statements.trigger: PLAY request with Scale header while in Play state
actions: send 200 OK with actual playback point and new scale

statements.subject: session
statements.description: There are two ways for the client to be informed about changes of media resources in Play state.

statements.subject: client
statements.description: The first being that the client will receive a PLAY_NOTIFY request with the Notify-Reason header set to media-properties-update. The client can use the value of the Media-Range header to decide further actions, if the Media-Range header is present in the PLAY_NOTIFY request.
actions: decide further actions based on Media-Range

statements.subject: client
statements.description: The second way is that the client issues a GET_PARAMETER request without a body but including a Media-Range header. The 200 OK response MUST include the current Media-Range header.
actions: send GET_PARAMETER request with Media-Range header and no body
receive 200 OK with current Media-Range header

statements.subject: session
statements.description: Dynamic on-demand media is indicated by the content of the Media-Properties header in the SETUP response when: the Random Access property is set to Random-Access; the Content Modifications property is set to Dynamic; the Retention property is set to Unlimited or Time-Limited.
statements.guard_semantics: classifies session as dynamic on-demand media

statements.subject: client
statements.description: A client MAY send PLAY requests without the Range header for live media.
statements.trigger: PLAY request (no Range header, live media)
actions: send PLAY request without Range header

statements.subject: client
statements.description: If the PLAY request includes the Range header for live media, it MUST use a symbolic value representing 'now'; for NPT, that range specification is 'npt=now-'.
statements.trigger: PLAY request (with Range header, live media)
actions: send PLAY request with Range header set to symbolic 'now' value (e.g., npt=now-)

statements.subject: server
statements.description: The server MUST include the Range header in the PLAY response, and it MUST indicate an explicit time value and not a symbolic value.
actions: include Range header with explicit time value (not symbolic)
express time since session start as open interval (e.g., npt=96.23-)

statements.subject: server
statements.description: For live media, the SETUP 200 OK response MUST include the Media-Range header.

statements.subject: session
statements.description: Live media with recording is indicated by the content of the Media-Properties header in the SETUP response when: the Random Access property is set to Random-Access; the Content Modifications property is set to Time-Progressing; the Retention property is set to Time-Limited or Unlimited.
statements.guard_semantics: media.random_access = Random-Access & media.content_modifications = Time-Progressing & media.retention = Time-Limited | media.retention = Unlimited

statements.subject: server
statements.description: The SETUP 200 OK response MUST include the Media-Range header for this type of media (live media with recording).
statements.guard_semantics: media.random_access = Random-Access & media.content_modifications = Time-Progressing & (media.retention = Time-Limited | media.retention = Unlimited)

statements.subject: server
statements.description: If the client requests a delivery point that is located outside the recording window, e.g., if the requested point is too far in the past, the server selects the oldest point in the recording.
statements.trigger: PLAY request with out-of-window delivery point
actions: adjust delivery point to oldest point in recording

statements.subject: server
statements.description: The SETUP 200 OK response MUST include the Media-Range header for live media with recording (Random-Access, Time-Progressing, Time-Duration properties).
statements.guard_semantics: media.random_access = Random-Access & media.content_modifications = Time-Progressing & media.retention = Time-Duration

statements.subject: server
statements.description: The server adjusts the play point to the requested border of the window, if the client requests a play point that is located outside the recording windows, e.g., if requested too far in the past, the server selects the oldest range in the recording.
statements.trigger: PLAY request with play point outside recording window
actions: adjust play point to nearest valid border of recording window

statements.subject: server
statements.description: The PLAY_NOTIFY method is issued by a server to inform a client about an asynchronous event for a session in Play state.
statements.trigger: asynchronous event occurs during Play state
actions: server sends PLAY_NOTIFY request with Session header

statements.subject: message
statements.description: The Session header MUST be presented in a PLAY_NOTIFY request and indicates the scope of the request.

statements.subject: client
statements.description: The client SHOULD immediately return a response to the server upon receiving PLAY_NOTIFY.

statements.subject: client
statements.description: In case the client does not understand the reason for the notification, it MUST respond with a 465 (Notification Reason Unknown) error code.
actions: client sends 465 Notification Reason Unknown response

statements.subject: message
statements.description: The Notify-Reason header specifies the reason why the server sends the PLAY_NOTIFY request.

statements.subject: server
statements.description: A PLAY_NOTIFY request with the Notify-Reason header set to end-of-stream indicates the completion or near completion of the PLAY request and the ending delivery of the media stream(s). The request MUST NOT be issued unless the server is in the Play state.
actions: include Request-Status header indicating which PLAY request and its completion status
include Range header with actual numeric end position

statements.description: In response to a client SETUP request where the setup parameter is set to 'active', a server's 2xx reply MUST assign the setup parameter to 'passive' on the Transport header line.
actions: assign setup=passive in Transport response header

statements.subject: server
statements.description: In response to a client SETUP request where the setup parameter is set to 'passive', a server's 2xx reply MUST assign the setup parameter to 'active' on the Transport header line.
actions: assign setup=active in Transport response header

statements.subject: server
statements.description: In response to a client SETUP request where the setup parameter is set to 'actpass', a server's 2xx reply MUST assign the setup parameter to 'active' or 'passive' on the Transport header line.
actions: assign setup=active or setup=passive in Transport response header

statements.subject: server
statements.description: If a client SETUP request assigns the 'new' value to 'connection', the server response MUST also assign the 'new' value to 'connection' on the Transport line.
actions: assign connection=new in Transport response header

statements.subject: server
statements.description: If a client SETUP request assigns the 'existing' value to 'connection', the server response MUST assign a value of 'existing' or 'new' to 'connection' on the Transport line, at its discretion.
actions: assign connection=existing or connection=new in Transport response header

statements.subject: session
statements.description: unicast / multicast: This parameter is a mutually exclusive indication of whether unicast or multicast delivery will be attempted. One of the two values MUST be specified.
statements.guard_semantics: exactly one of unicast or multicast must appear per transport-spec

statements.subject: session
statements.description: The argument provides the channel number to be used in the $ block and MUST be present [when interleaved parameter is specified].

statements.subject: transaction
statements.description: The ssrc parameter MUST NOT be specified in requests.

statements.subject: transaction
statements.description: Note that the 'holdconn' value for setup is not defined for RTSP use, and MUST NOT appear on a Transport line.

statements.subject: server
statements.description: The Transport header MAY also be used in subsequent SETUP requests to change transport parameters. A server MAY refuse to change parameters of an existing stream.
statements.trigger: subsequent SETUP request to change transport parameters
actions: or refuse change of parameters for existing stream

statements.subject: server
statements.description: When a client tries to set up an insecure channel to the server (using the 'rtsp' URI), and the policy for the resource requires a secure channel, the server MUST redirect the client to the secure service by sending a 301 redirect response code together with the correct Location URI (using the 'rtsps' scheme).
actions: set Location URI with rtsps scheme

statements.subject: client
statements.description: A user or client MAY upgrade a non secured URI to a secured by changing the scheme from 'rtsp' to 'rtsps'. A server implementing support for 'rtsps' MUST allow this.
actions: change URI scheme from rtsp to rtsps

statements.subject: connection
statements.description: The RTSP agent having the TCP/TLS connection MUST verify that the server certificate associated with the connection has a SubjectAltName matching the hostname present in the URI for the resource an RTSP request is to be issued.
statements.guard_semantics: SubjectAltName must match hostname in request URI before reusing existing TCP/TLS connection

statements.subject: server
statements.description: If the policy does not accept the credentials of the next hop, the proxy MUST respond with a message using status code 471 (Connection Credentials Not Accepted).

statements.subject: server
statements.description: If no such transport connection exists at the time when the server desires to send the request, the server MUST discard the message.

statements.subject: server
statements.description: If the server-to-client request is in relation to a session established over a TLS secured channel, it MUST be sent in a TLS secured connection. That secured connection MUST also be the one used by the last client-to-server request.

statements.subject: server
statements.description: Each proxy MUST set up the TLS session to the next hop if not already present (i.e., run the TLS handshake, but do not send the RTSP request).
statements.trigger: RTSP request received and TLS session not yet established
actions: run TLS handshake to next hop

statements.subject: server
statements.description: Check if a matching identity and hash of the peer certificate are present in the Accept-Credentials header. If present, send the message to the next hop and conclude these procedures.
statements.trigger: matching identity and hash found in Accept-Credentials header
actions: forward RTSP request to next hop

statements.subject: server
statements.description: The proxy responds to the RTSP request with a 470 or 407 response code when no matching identity and hash are present in the Accept-Credentials header. The proxy MUST include a Connection-Credentials header with the next hop's identity and certificate.
statements.trigger: no matching identity and hash found in Accept-Credentials header
actions: send 470 or 407 response with Connection-Credentials header

statements.subject: client
statements.description: The client MUST upon receiving a 470 (Connection Authorization Required) or 407 (Proxy Authentication Required) response with Connection-Credentials header take the decision on whether or not to accept the certificate.
statements.trigger: 470 or 407 response with Connection-Credentials header received

statements.subject: client
statements.description: If the certificate is accepted, the client has to again send the RTSP request. In that request, the client has to include the Accept-Credentials header including the hash over the DER-encoded certificate for all trusted proxies in the chain.
actions: include Accept-Credentials header with DER-encoded certificate hash for all trusted proxies

statements.subject: message
statements.description: In the 470 or 407 response message the proxy MUST include a Connection-Credentials header with the next hop's identity and certificate.

statements.subject: message
statements.description: The client has to include the Accept-Credentials header including the hash over the DER-encoded certificate for all trusted proxies in the chain when resending the RTSP request after accepting the certificate.

statements.subject: session
statements.description: Init: Initial state, no session exists.

statements.subject: session
statements.description: Ready: Session is ready to start playing.

statements.subject: session
statements.description: Play: Session is playing, i.e., sending media-stream data in the direction S->C.

statements.subject: session
statements.description: NRM: The number of media streams that are part of this session.

statements.subject: session
statements.description: RP: Resume point, the point in the presentation time line at which a request to continue playing will resume from.

statements.subject: session
statements.description: SETUP in Init state (no redirect needed): transitions to Ready; sets NRM=1, RP=0.0.

statements.subject: session
statements.description: SETUP in Init state where Needs Redirect: state remains Init, 3rr Redirect response.

statements.subject: session
statements.description: S->C: REDIRECT with No Session header in Init state: terminate all sessions, state remains Init.

statements.subject: session
statements.description: SETUP with New URI in Ready state: state remains Ready, NRM+=1.

statements.subject: session
statements.description: SETUP with URI already set up prior in Ready state: state remains Ready, change transport param.

statements.subject: session
statements.description: TEARDOWN with Prs URI in Ready state: transitions to Init, no session hdr, NRM=0.

statements.subject: session
statements.description: TEARDOWN with md URI and NRM=1 in Ready state: transitions to Init, no session hdr, NRM=0.

statements.subject: session
statements.description: TEARDOWN with md URI and NRM>1 in Ready state: state remains Ready, Session hdr, NRM-=1.

statements.subject: session
statements.description: PLAY with Prs URI and No range in Ready state: transitions to Play, play from RP.
statements.pre_cond: session.state = Ready & request.uri = presentation_uri & request.range = absent

statements.subject: session
statements.description: PLAY with Prs URI and Range in Ready state: transitions to Play, according to range.
statements.pre_cond: session.state = Ready & request.uri = presentation_uri & request.range = present

statements.subject: session
statements.description: PLAY with md URI, NRM=1, Range in Ready state: transitions to Play, according to range.
statements.pre_cond: session.state = Ready & request.uri = media_uri & session.NRM = 1 & request.range = present

statements.subject: session
statements.description: PLAY with md URI and NRM=1 (no range) in Ready state: transitions to Play, play from RP.
statements.pre_cond: session.state = Ready & request.uri = media_uri & session.NRM = 1 & request.range = absent

statements.subject: session
statements.description: PAUSE with Prs URI in Ready state: state remains Ready, return PP.

statements.subject: session
statements.description: SC:REDIRECT with Terminate-Reason in Ready state: state remains Ready, Set RedP.

statements.subject: session
statements.description: SC:REDIRECT with No Terminate-Reason time parameter in Ready state: transitions to Init, session is removed.

statements.subject: session
statements.description: Timeout in Ready state: transitions to Init.

statements.subject: session
statements.description: RedP reached in Ready state: transitions to Init, TEARDOWN of session.

statements.subject: session
statements.description: PAUSE with Prs URI in Play state: transitions to Ready, set RP to present point.

statements.subject: session
statements.description: End of media (all media finished) in Play state: state remains Play, set RP = End of media.

statements.subject: session
statements.description: End of range in Play state: state remains Play, set RP = End of range.

statements.subject: session
statements.description: PLAY with Prs URI, No range in Play state: state remains Play, play from present point.
statements.pre_cond: session.state = Play & request.uri = presentation_uri & request.range = absent

statements.subject: session
statements.description: PLAY with Prs URI, Range in Play state: state remains Play, according to range.
statements.pre_cond: session.state = Play & request.uri = presentation_uri & request.range = present

statements.subject: session
statements.description: SC:PLAY_NOTIFY in Play state: state remains Play, response 200.

statements.subject: session
statements.description: SETUP with New URI in Play state: state remains Play, response 455.

statements.subject: session
statements.description: SETUP with md URI (not IFI) in Play state: state remains Play, response 455.
statements.pre_cond: session.state = Play & request.uri = media_uri & feature.implemented = false

statements.subject: session
statements.description: SETUP with md URI, IFI (If Implemented) in Play state: state remains Play, change transport param.
statements.pre_cond: session.state = Play & request.uri = media_uri & feature.implemented = true

statements.subject: session
statements.description: TEARDOWN with Prs URI in Play state: transitions to Init, no session hdr.

statements.subject: session
statements.description: TEARDOWN with md URI and NRM=1 in Play state: transitions to Init, no session hdr, NRM=0.

statements.subject: session
statements.description: TEARDOWN with md URI (NRM>1) in Play state: state remains Play, response 455.

statements.subject: session
statements.description: SC:REDIRECT with Terminate Reason with Time parameter in Play state: state remains Play, Set RedP.

statements.subject: session
statements.description: SC:REDIRECT without Terminate Reason time parameter in Play state: transitions to Init, session is removed.

statements.subject: session
statements.description: RedP reached in Play state: transitions to Init, TEARDOWN of session.

statements.subject: session
statements.description: Timeout in Play state: transitions to Init, stop media playout.

statements.subject: session
statements.description: A response code of 3rr will result in the session being ended and its state changed to Init.

statements.subject: session
statements.description: An unrecoverable error results in the ending of the session.

statements.subject: client
statements.description: After sending (receiving) a 2xx reply for a SETUP method for a non-interleaved RTP/AVP/TCP media stream, the active party SHOULD initiate the TCP connection as soon as possible.
statements.trigger: 2xx reply for SETUP (non-interleaved RTP/AVP/TCP) sent or received

statements.subject: client
statements.description: The client MUST NOT send a PLAY request prior to the establishment of all the TCP connections negotiated using SETUP for the session.

statements.subject: server
statements.description: In case the server receives a PLAY request in a session that has not yet established all the TCP connections, it MUST respond using the 464 (Data Transport Not Ready Yet) error code.
actions: respond 464 Data Transport Not Ready Yet

statements.subject: session
statements.description: A successful PAUSE request for media being transported over RTP/AVP/TCP pauses the flow of packets over the connections, without closing the connections.
actions: pause packet flow over TCP connections

statements.subject: session
statements.description: A successful TEARDOWN request signals that the TCP connections for RTP and RTCP are to be closed by the RTSP client as soon as possible.
actions: close TCP connections for RTP and RTCP

statements.subject: server
statements.description: If all transport specs require SRTP but no MIKEY parameter or other supported keying method is included, the server SHALL respond with 403 (Forbidden).

statements.subject: server
statements.description: A transport spec using SRTP and MIKEY is selected but an error is encountered in the MIKEY processing. In this case, an RTSP error response code of 466 (Key Management Error) SHALL be used.
statements.trigger: MIKEY processing error on SETUP request
statements.pre_cond: setup.transport_spec_uses_srtp = true & setup.transport_spec_uses_mikey = true & mikey.processing_error = true

statements.subject: client
statements.description: The client receives the SETUP response and, if the response code indicates a successful request, it decodes the MIKEY message and establishes the SRTP cryptographic context from the parameters in the MIKEY response.
statements.trigger: 2xx SETUP response with MIKEY parameter received

statements.subject: session
statements.description: RTCP traffic from the RTSP client to the RTSP server MUST function as keep-alive. This requires an RTSP server supporting RTP to use the received RTCP packets as indications that the client desires the related RTSP session to be kept alive.

statements.subject: client
statements.description: The client forms the MIKEY Initiator message using RSA-R mode in unicast mode. The MIKEY message is base64-encoded and becomes the value of the MIKEY parameter included in the transport specification(s) specifying an SRTP-based profile (SAVP, SAVPF) in the SETUP request.
statements.trigger: SETUP request for SRTP-based profile (SAVP or SAVPF)
actions: form MIKEY Initiator message (RSA-R unicast mode)
include MIKEY parameter in SETUP request transport specification

statements.subject: session
statements.description: SETUP requests may include this identifier in the If-Match field (see Section 18.24) to allow session establishment only if this attribute value still corresponds to that of the current description.
statements.guard_semantics: session establishment proceeds only when session_description.mtag = If-Match.value

statements.subject: session
statements.description: SETUP requests may include this identifier in the If-Match field to allow session establishment only if this attribute value still corresponds to that of the current description.
statements.trigger: SETUP request with If-Match header containing mtag value

statements.subject: client
statements.description: C->M: DESCRIBE rtsp://example.com/movie RTSP/2.0 ... M->C: RTSP/2.0 200 OK ... Content-Type: application/sdp
actions: server returns SDP in 200 OK response body

statements.subject: session
statements.description: The presence of a session-level control attribute MUST be interpreted as support for aggregated control.
statements.guard_semantics: session.aggregate_control_supported = true when session-level a=control is present

statements.subject: client
statements.description: Note that the position of the control URI in the description implies that the client establishes separate RTSP control sessions to the servers audio.example.com and video.example.com.
statements.trigger: SDP received with no session-level a=control attribute
actions: client establishes separate RTSP control sessions per media stream

statements.subject: client
statements.description: In this scenario, the server has multiple streams that can be controlled as a whole. In this case, there are both a media-level 'a=control' attribute ... and a session-level 'a=control' attribute ... the client is recommended to establish a single RTSP session to the server.
statements.trigger: SDP received with session-level a=control attribute
actions: client establishes single RTSP session for aggregate control

statements.subject: server
statements.description: The behavior in the server when a Play is received in Play state has changed. Any new PLAY request now takes effect immediately replacing the previous request.
actions: replace current PLAY with new PLAY request immediately

statements.subject: session
statements.description: when a client closes its connection, the server may remove the RTSP session

statements.subject: server
statements.description: If the server chooses not to support RFC 2326, it MUST respond with a 505 (RTSP Version Not Supported) status code. A server MUST NOT respond to an RTSP 1.0 request with an RTSP 2.0 response.
actions: send 505 RTSP Version Not Supported response

statements.subject: client
statements.description: Clients implementing RTSP 2.0 MAY use an OPTIONS request with an RTSP-Version of 'RTSP/2.0' to determine whether a server supports RTSP 2.0. If the server responds with either an RTSP-Version of 'RTSP/1.0' or a status code of 505, the client will have to use RTSP 1.0 requests.
statements.trigger: OPTIONS response received with RTSP/1.0 version or 505 status
actions: downgrade to RTSP 1.0 for subsequent requests
